walkthroughs.body_html:
Changes in Medicine c1848-c1948 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Changes in Medicine c1848-c1948 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Changes in Medicine c1848-c1948.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who first developed the smallpox vaccine in 1796?
options: Louis Pasteur
Edward Jenner
Robert Koch
John Snow

mcqs.q: Which pump did John Snow link to cholera in 1854?
options: Broad Street
Oxford Street
Soho Square
Fleet Street

mcqs.q: Why was Vesalius significant in the history of medicine?
options: His 1543 De Humani Corporis Fabrica corrected Galen's errors via human dissection and accurate illustration, founding modern anatomy though not curing disease.
Vesalius invented the microscope.
Vesalius discovered the cause of disease and ended humoral theory.
The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.

mcqs.q: How did the feudal system work in Norman England?
options: Feudalism was a written constitution introduced by William in 1066.
The king granted land to tenants-in-chief in return for knight service; they in turn enfeoffed knights who held land in return for military service to their lord.
Vesalius invented the microscope.
Feudalism meant peasants were slaves owned by the king.

mcqs.q: What was the theory of the four humours?
options: Disease was caused by imbalance of blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile; treatment aimed to rebalance them via bloodletting, purging or diet. It dominated for nearly 2,000 years.
The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.
Medieval doctors knew about germs but used humours because they had no medicine.
Vesalius invented the microscope.
